 This is an Expo/React Native mobile application. Prioritize mobile-first patterns, performance, and cross-platform compatibility.
 
 # Pokedex+
 
 The Pokedex+ is an upgraded version of the pokedex. It is an index containing all the pokemon from every generation, including shinies. Every pokémon has a detail page. For people who want to get the best out of their pokemon.
 
 It runs on the PokeAPI (`https://pokeapi.co/api/v2/`)
 
 ## Commands
 
 Use `npx`
 
 ```bash
 npx expo install <package>  # ALWAYS use instead of npm/yarn/pnpm/bun add — resolves SDK-compatible versions
 npx expo start              # start the dev server
 npx expo lint               # lint
 npx tsc --noEmit            # typecheck
 npx expo-doctor             # diagnose dependency and config issues
 npx expo install --fix      # fix incompatible package versions
 ```
 
 Run lint and typecheck before declaring any task done.
 
 ## Navigation & Routing
 
 - Use **Expo Router** for all navigation. Routes live in `src/app/` — every file there is a screen, `_layout.tsx` files define navigators. Keep non-route code (components, hooks, utils) outside `src/app/`.
 - Import `Link`, `router`, and `useLocalSearchParams` from `expo-router`.
 - Docs: https://docs.expo.dev/router/introduction.md
 
 ## Building with EAS
 
 Use EAS to build, sign, and submit the app in the cloud (`eas build`, `eas submit`) and to ship over-the-air updates (`eas update`) — no local Xcode or Android Studio required. Run EAS CLI as `bunx eas-cli <command>` in Bun projects, or `npx eas-cli@latest <command>` otherwise; substitute that for bare `eas` in docs examples.
 Docs: https://docs.expo.dev/eas/index.md
 
 ## Rules
 
 - If `ios/` and `android/` directories do not exist, they are generated (Continuous Native Generation). Never create or edit them by hand — configure native behavior in `app.json` and config plugins.
 - Expo Go only includes its bundled native modules. After adding a library with native code, the app needs a development build: `npx expo run:ios|android` locally, or `eas build --profile development`.
 - Prefer recommended Expo modules over third-party libraries, and check your available skills before adding dependencies. Docs: https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/index.md
 - Follow the Figma design consistently across all screens and components.
 - Keep the alignment, positioning, and spacing of repeated UI elements consistent.
 
 ## Existing Project
 
 - Inspect the existing project before making changes.
 - Reuse existing components, hooks, utilities and architecture when needed.
 - Do not recreate working functionality when it's not needed.
 - Do not replace the existing application with a new project.
 - Explain significant architectural changes before implementing them.
 
 ## API
 
 - Use PokéAPI as the source of Pokémon data.
 - Follow the official PokéAPI documentation.
 - Understand the difference between `/pokemon/` and `/pokemon-species/`.
 - Fetch additional Pokémon data only when needed.
 - Handle API failures, missing data and unavailable sprites.
 - Do not assume optional API fields are always populated.
 - Avoid unnecessary API requests and duplicate data fetching.
 
 ## Database
 
 - Use SQLite for persistent local data.
 - Follow the database structure defined in the project specifications.
 - Keep Pokémon API data separate from user-specific data such as Favorites.
 - Use database migrations when changing an existing database structure.
 - Do not store information locally if it can be derived reliably from existing data.
 
 ## Code Quality
 
 - Reuse the code language from existing project.
 - Prefer reusable components and hooks.
 - Keep components focused on a single responsibility.
 - Use meaningful, adhd/asd-friendly variable and function names, but don't make it too long.
 - Add adhd/asd-friendly comments when they explain non-obvious logic or important decisions.
 - Do not add comments that simply repeat what the code already says.
 - Avoid unnecessary dependencies.
 - When implementing a feature, explain the important parts of the implementation in plain language. Explain what the code does, how the components work together, and why important technical decisions were made. Do not explain every line unless asked.

 # Favorites List
 
 ## Goal
 
 Browse and manage a personal list of favorite Pokémon, then open a favorite’s detail page or share it.
 
 ## Context
 
 - The home screen has a Pokémon tab and a Favorites tab. Favorites is a tab, not a separate detail route.
 - The Favorites tab screen is `src/app/(tabs)/favorites.tsx`.
 - Pokémon details use `src/app/pokemon/[id].tsx`.
 - The Pokémon index, card behavior, regional forms, and sprite toggle are specified in `specs/features/pokedex-list.md`.
 - The Pokémon detail and evolution-chain loading and error behavior are specified in `specs/features/pokedex-detail.md`.
 - Favorites are user-specific data stored on the phone in SQLite, separately from Pokémon API data. Use the `personal_list` table defined in `specs/product.md`.
 - Pokémon data comes from the PokeAPI (`https://pokeapi.co/api/v2/pokemon`).
 - Use the existing theme in `src/constants/theme.ts`, the Rubik font files in `assets/fonts` loaded with Expo Font, and no new dependencies.
 
 ## Constraints
 
 - Show only Pokémon the user has added to Favorites.
 - The Favorites list is the screen for this tab; do not add a separate detail screen for the Favorites feature.
 
 ## Requirements
 
 ### Favorites list
 
 - Display two Pokémon cards per row.
 - Each card shows the Pokédex number, sprite, name, and a three-dot menu.
 - Tapping a card opens that Pokémon’s detail page.
 - Show an empty state with the text “No favorites yet” when the user has not saved any Pokémon. Do not show a button in this state.
 - If saved Pokémon exist but none match the active filters or name search, show no cards, message, or button. Keep the controls available so the user can change or clear them.
 - Show a loading state while the Favorites list loads. If loading fails, show an error state and let the user retry.
 - Keep each favorite after the app closes and restarts. A Pokémon can appear in Favorites only once.
 - Keep the selected sorting and filters when the user opens a Pokémon’s detail page and returns. Keep search text as specified in `specs/features/pokedex-search.md`.
 
 ### Sorting and filters
 
 - Sort by Pokédex ID or name, in ascending or descending order. Initially sort by Pokédex ID, descending.
 - Provide filters for generation, rarity, type, and name. Apply filters only to saved Pokémon.
 - Use the same filter behavior as `specs/features/pokedex-list.md`: multiple values may be selected within a filter, a Pokémon must match at least one selected value within every active filter, and must match every active filter. Filters do not change sort order.
 - Rarity includes Pokémon marked legendary or mythical by their species data.
 - Name filtering follows the case-insensitive, two-letter minimum behavior in `specs/features/pokedex-search.md`.
 
 ### Card actions and navigation
 
 - The three-dot menu contains “Open Pokémon”, “Remove from favorites”, and “Share”.
 - “Open Pokémon” opens the Pokémon’s detail page.
 - Tapping “Remove from favorites” removes that Pokémon immediately and briefly provides an “Undo” action. Undo restores the favorite. The user can also add it again from the Pokémon tab or its detail page.
 - “Share” opens the phone’s share sheet with the Pokémon’s name and Pokédex number as text.
 - Use the regional form selection and regular/shiny toggle behavior specified in `specs/features/pokedex-list.md`. Pass the selected form and shiny setting to the detail page, as required by that spec.
 - Use the detail page’s favorite control to add or remove the current Pokémon, and keep the Favorites list up to date when returning to it.
 
 ### Related detail behavior
 
 - Pokémon detail and evolution-chain loading and error states are specified in `specs/features/pokedex-detail.md`.
 
 ## Acceptance Criteria
 
 - [ ] Favorites appears as a home tab alongside the Pokémon tab.
 - [ ] The list contains only saved Pokémon, displays two cards per row, and starts in descending Pokédex ID order.
 - [ ] Users can sort by Pokédex ID or name, ascending or descending, and filter by generation, rarity, type, and name using the Pokémon index rules.
 - [ ] Each card opens its Pokémon detail page when tapped and provides the specified three-dot actions.
 - [ ] Adding and removing a favorite updates the list, and saved favorites survive an app restart.
 - [ ] An empty Favorites list shows “No favorites yet” without a button.
 - [ ] If saved Pokémon do not match the current filters or search, the list shows no cards, message, or button, and the controls remain available.
 - [ ] Opening a Pokémon and returning preserves the selected sorting and filters.
 - [ ] Removing a favorite takes effect immediately and offers a temporary Undo action.
 - [ ] Loading and retryable error states are provided for the list; detail and evolution-chain states follow the detail feature spec.
 - [ ] The design font is loaded with Expo Font from `assets/fonts`.
 
 ## Out of Scope
 
 - Filtering by color.

 # Pokedex+
 
 The Pokedex+ is an upgraded version of the pokedex. It is an index containing all the pokemon from every generation, including shinies. Every pokémon has a detail page. For people who want to get the best out of their pokemon.
 
 ## Core action
 
 Pick a pokémon and see it's information
 
 ## Features
 
 <One line per feature, linking to its file in `specs/features/`. 3 to 6, not
 more. Each one becomes a GitHub issue.>
 
 1. [Normal list](./features/pokédex-index.md) Browse an index of normal pokémon
 2. [Search by name](./features/pokédex-search.md) Search pokémon by name
 3. [Pokémon detail](./features/pokédex-detail.md) See general info, stats, and evolution of a pokémon
 4. [Favorites list](./features/pokédex-favorites.md) Browse an index of shiny pokémon
 5. [Pokémon Comparison] (./features/pokédex-compare.md) Put two Pokémon side by side and sees who is stronger on which stat.
 6. [Catching-simulator] (./features/pokédex-simulator.md) Simulate catching a pokémon (in multiple conditions) with a list of usable pokéballs.
 
 ## Data
 
 - **API**: PokeApi, no login, no key
 - **Endpoints**:
   /pokemon?limit=2000 — Fetch the complete Pokémon index.
   /pokemon/{id or name} — Fetch Pokémon information, including stats, types and sprites.
   /pokemon-species/{id} — Fetch species information and evolution-chain URL.
   /item-category/33/ — Fetch special balls
   /item-category/34/ — Fetch standard balls
 - **Stored on the phone**:
   Table pokemon in SQLite: id (PokéAPI Pokémon resource ID), species_id (PokéAPI species ID), name, height, weight, base_experience, types_json, abilities_json, stats_json, sprites_json, forms_json, generation, capture_rate, updated_at. Each base Pokémon and each listed regional, Mega, or Gigantamax variant is a separate row with its own Pokémon resource ID. `forms_json` stores related form metadata, including Pokémon resource IDs and available regular/shiny sprite references.
   Table personal_list: personal_list_id, pokemon_id (PokéAPI Pokémon resource ID), created_at. Each variant can be favorited independently.
 
 ## Technical choices
 
 <Fill in the two below: every app makes these choices. For each one: what
 you picked, what else you could have done, and why. Write it before you
 build. If you change your mind later, change it here too.>
 
 - **Stored in SQLite**: It allows for local, persistent storage and structured queries, which is similar to SQL and I am more familiar with. I don't have enough knowledge about AsyncStorage.
 - **Native feature**: Share on your favorites tab. Share your favorite pokémon with your friends.
 
 ## Technical core
 
 <Tick these off as you build. They are required for a pass.>
 
 - [ ] Runs in Expo Go
 - [ ] Live data through TanStack Query
 - [ ] At least 2 screens with Expo Router
 - [ ] Something in SQLite that survives a restart
 - [ ] Loading and error state on every load
 - [ ] One native feature: Share favorites, in the favorites tab
 - [ ] TypeScript and ESLint without errors
 - [ ] UI, data and logic in separate files
 
 ## Optional
 
 <Tick the ones you built, +0.5 each. Delete the rest or leave them unticked.>
 
 - [ ] Three different Reanimated animations, each with a purpose
 - [ ] Dark mode: every screen looks right, all colours from the theme
 - [ ] Pagination: page by page while you scroll, not all at once
 - [ ] Clean TypeScript: no `any`, no `as` casts, no `@ts-ignore`
 - [ ] Design (not Pokédex): a consistent own style with your own font
 - [ ] Localization: two languages
 - [ ] No warnings: no `console.log`, none in the terminal or on screen
 - [ ] Tests: one per feature on the logic, `npm test` passes
 - [ ] CI: lint and tsc on every push
 - [ ] Accessibility: button labels, largest text size
 - [ ] Optimistic update
 
 ## Out of scope
 
 accounts

 # Pokémon Detail Page
 
 ## Context
 
 - The detail screen is `src/app/pokemon/[id].tsx`; it opens from a Pokémon card.
 - Pokémon data comes from PokeAPI `/pokemon/{id}` and `/pokemon-species/{id}`. The species response supplies the evolution-chain URL.
 - The list screen, including its regional-form picker and shiny toggle, is specified in `specs/features/pokedex-list.md`.
 - Favorites are stored in SQLite in the `personal_list` table defined in `specs/product.md`.
 - Use Expo Router, the existing theme in `src/constants/theme.ts`, the Rubik font files in `assets/fonts`, and no new dependencies.
 
 ## Goals
 
 - Let the user inspect a Pokémon's identifying information, general information, stats, and evolution family.
 - Let the user manage that Pokémon in Favorites and open its catching simulator.
 
 ## Requirements
 
 ### Detail screen
 
 - Show the selected Pokémon's name, Pokédex ID, type badges, and sprite.
 - Open with the form and regular/shiny setting selected on the Pokémon list. The user can also change the form and regular/shiny setting on the detail screen.
 - Keep form selection independent from the regular/shiny setting. Offer the regional forms specified in `specs/features/pokedex-list.md`; show the shiny control only when the selected form has a shiny sprite.
 - When returning to the list, keep the form and regular/shiny setting most recently selected on the detail screen.
 - Provide a back button that returns to the screen that opened the detail page.
 - Provide a Favorite control that adds or removes this Pokémon from the user's SQLite Favorites. The control reflects whether it is currently saved.
 - Provide a “Catch” button that opens `src/app/pokemon/simulator/[id].tsx` for the selected Pokémon. Catching behavior is specified separately in `specs/features/pokedex-simulator.md`.
 
 ### Tabs
 
 - Provide “About”, “Stats”, and “Evolution” tabs. “About” is selected when the detail screen first opens.
 - Clearly indicate which tab is selected.
 
 #### About
 
 - Show the Pokémon's name, Pokédex ID, base experience as `Base {base_experience}XP`, weight in kilograms, height in meters, types, and abilities.
 
 #### Stats
 
 - Show HP, Attack, Defense, Special Attack, Special Defense, and Speed.
 - For each stat, show its label, a bar, and its numeric value.
 - Use a fixed scale from 0 to 255 for every stat bar.
 
 #### Evolution
 
 - Show cards for the selected Pokémon's complete evolution family: earlier and later stages, all branches, and the selected Pokémon itself.
 - Show Mega forms when they are present in the available PokeAPI data.
 - Each card shows a sprite, name, and Pokédex ID. For Pokémon with gender-differentiated sprites, show the regular sprite and both male (♂) and female (♀) symbols.
 - Visually highlight the card for the Pokémon whose detail page is open, using an accent border.
 - Tapping another Pokémon's card opens that Pokémon's detail page.
 - If the selected Pokémon has no other evolutionary forms, show only its own card without an error or additional message.
 
 ### Type colors and missing data
 
 - Give each Pokémon type a distinct, fixed badge color and keep badge text legible against its background. Use the existing theme for other colors and spacing.
 - If an optional text value is missing, show “Not available”. If a sprite is missing, show a neutral placeholder; do not treat either case as a request failure.
 
 ### Loading and errors
 
 - Show a loading state while the Pokémon's detail data loads.
 - Show an error state with a retry action when detail data cannot be loaded.
 - Show loading and retryable error states for the evolution family independently of the rest of the detail screen.
 
 ### Visual design
 
 - Use the app's Rubik font, loaded with Expo Font from `assets/fonts`.
 - Use the app's theme colors and spacing from `src/constants/theme.ts`.
 
 ## Acceptance Criteria
 
 - [ ] Opening a Pokémon shows its name, ID, type badges, selected form and regular/shiny sprite, with controls to change the form and sprite setting.
